title: Six-class secp256k1 rho with kappa=1.01 on the repriced 752-step ledger (126.3231)

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack described in proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^126.3231 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). Subject to the explicit H1 heuristic (slowdown allowance kappa=1.01, floor p0=0.3950 at S_ops/kappa) and the upstream cost/event estimates, recovery probability is greater than 0.3908 and therefore at least 0.39. Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. The walk, counted AArch64 kernels (111 + 523 instructions), repriced step (752 instructions = 0.752 units, 634 counted + 118 analytic rows), doubling (0.956), traversal (0.776) and specified report store are the public repriced six-class package credited in upstream-proof.md. The only numerical changes are the H1 calibration kappa=1.01 / p0=0.3950 from the public kappa101 q29 census and the re-optimized hard cap. Exact ledger: phase 1 = 2^126.3146672, hard extras < 2^107.1556, Markov allowance 2^118.89504, total W_ledger = 2^126.3230715, claim 126.3231 = 1263231/10000; success = 0.3950 - 0.00416 - 2e-7 = 0.3908398 > 0.3908 > 0.39. The claim is self-contained in proof.md; no prior acceptance, review verdict, official score or cross-submission comparison is a premise. The design is credited as provenance only; no dependency link is declared. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break or executed production attack.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and truncated canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled sequential toy pipeline on configured subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with an unreduced subgroup-order check, a T_c census, node routing, and a long-trail trap test; kernels: limb-for-limb Python ports of the field kernels checked against big integers and affine secp256k1, instruction counts parsed from the shipped AArch64 assembly, the shipped loops executed by an interpreter, and the work-meter ledger recomputed from the prices and rows of proof.md section 5. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
